metaDescription: Six cordless circular saws compared on blade size, brushless motors, depth of cut, bevel range and battery platform for framing, decking and trim.
expertTake: The DeWalt DCS590B is the cordless circular saw most carpenters should buy, with a brushless motor, up to 1,700 MWO and a 2-9/16 inch depth of cut. The Craftsman CMCS551B is the value pick for homeowners on the V20 platform. If you rip long sheets of 3/4 inch plywood all day, skip cordless and buy a corded sidewinder or worm drive, because a battery saw spends its charge fast on sustained rips.
introParagraphs: A cordless circular saw trades the cord for a battery pack, and the trade is real: the saw can cut anywhere, but every long cut spends charge. Blade size, motor type and battery capacity decide how much work you get done before the pack runs flat.
This guide explains how brushless motors, blade diameter and bevel range change daily use, why battery platform matters more than the saw itself and where light saws fall short.

products.name: DeWalt DCS590B 20V MAX XR Brushless 7-1/4 Inch Circular Saw
products.description:
The DCS590B is DeWalt's most powerful 20V MAX circular saw, quoting up to 1,700 MWO (maximum watts out) and 5,500 rpm no load. A brushless motor claims up to 368 cuts per charge in the maker's test. The 7-1/4 inch blade cuts 2-9/16 inches deep at 90 degrees, so it handles a 2x4 and a 4x4 in one pass.

It is a bare tool, so you must pair it with a large battery to get the best from it. Compared with the FlexVolt DCS578B it is lighter and uses the standard 20V MAX packs, but the FlexVolt has more raw power. Against the Craftsman CMCS551B it offers stronger sustained cutting.

Magnesium and metal parts keep the shoe flat over years. Check the blade guard return, clean the sawdust from the vent and use a sharp blade. Pair it with a 24 tooth framing blade for lumber and a 40 tooth blade for plywood.
products.bestFor: Carpenters and serious DIYers who want corded power from a battery.
pros: Up to 1,700 MWO from a brushless motor
cons: Sold bare, so batteries add cost

products.name: DeWalt DCS578B FlexVolt 60V MAX 7-1/4 Inch Circular Saw with Brake
products.description:
The FlexVolt DCS578B claims up to 47 percent more power than its predecessor, and it uses the FlexVolt battery that switches between 20V and 60V. An electric brake stops the blade quickly after the trigger is released. Maximum bevel capacity is 57 degrees, with stops at 22.5 and 45 degrees.

It is the choice for sustained cutting in dense lumber, where the DCS590B starts to labor. It is heavier, and the FlexVolt batteries cost more. Compared with the Milwaukee M18 saw it offers a larger battery option and more rated power.

Use it for framing, decking and ripping. Keep the blade sharp and the shoe clean. FlexVolt packs can also power other DeWalt 60V tools, which helps justify their cost.
products.bestFor: Framers and builders cutting dense lumber all day.
pros: Electric brake stops the blade quickly

products.name: Milwaukee M18 Brushless 7-1/4 Inch Circular Saw
products.description:
The Milwaukee M18 7-1/4 inch saw uses a brushless motor, an electric brake and magnesium upper and lower guards, which reduce weight and add durability. A rafter hook and an integrated dust port on the guard are practical touches. An LED light brightens the cut line.

Compared with the DeWalt DCS590B it is a close rival in features, and the choice usually depends on which battery platform you own. It is not as powerful as the FlexVolt DCS578B. It is a good choice for existing M18 owners who want a pro grade saw.

Keep the guards clean and check the brake. A fresh blade makes more difference than any motor spec. The rafter hook makes it easy to hang the saw on a joist between cuts.
products.bestFor: Milwaukee M18 owners who want a durable cordless saw.
pros: Magnesium guards save weight and last
Electric brake stops the blade fast
Rafter hook helps storage on site
cons: M18 batteries are not shared with DeWalt

products.name: Craftsman V20 RP CMCS551B Brushless 7-1/4 Inch Circular Saw
products.description:
The Craftsman CMCS551B is a brushless 7-1/4 inch saw with a maximum bevel of 56 degrees and positive stops at 22.5 and 45 degrees. The maker claims up to 75 percent more power than its brushed predecessor. An LED lights the cutting line.

It costs less than the DeWalt and Milwaukee saws, and it shares batteries with the V20 line. For homeowners cutting plywood, decking and 2x4 lumber it does the job. It is not meant for all day framing.

It is a bare tool, so plan for a 4 Ah battery. Keep the shoe clean and the blade sharp. Buying two blades, one rough and one fine, doubles what this saw can do.
products.bestFor: Homeowners on the Craftsman V20 platform.
pros: Brushless motor at a lower cost

products.name: Makita XSH03Z 18V LXT Brushless 6-1/2 Inch Circular Saw
products.description:
The Makita XSH03Z uses a 6-1/2 inch blade, which is lighter and handier than a 7-1/4 inch saw. A brushless motor delivers 5,000 rpm, and Automatic Speed Change adjusts speed and torque during the cut. The smaller blade means less depth of cut.

Compared with the Milwaukee M18 6-1/2 inch saw it is quicker at 5,000 rpm against 3,500 rpm. It is excellent for trim, plywood and decking. For deep structural cuts a 7-1/4 inch saw is better.

It is a bare tool, and Makita LXT batteries are widely used. Keep the base plate clean and the blade guard moving freely. The smaller size makes it a good second saw to keep in the truck.
products.bestFor: Trim carpenters and anyone who wants a lighter saw.
pros: Automatic Speed Change adapts to the cut
cons: Less depth of cut than 7-1/4 inch saws

products.name: 6-1/2 Inch Brushless Cordless Circular Saw with Two 4.0 Ah Batteries
products.description:
This unbranded 6-1/2 inch saw uses a 21V outer rotor brushless motor at 7,000 rpm, with cutting depths of 2-1/4 inches at 90 degrees and 1-7/16 inches at 45 degrees. It ships with two 4.0 Ah batteries and a fast charger. The LED helps show the line.

The speed is high, and the depth is modest, which fits light work in plywood and 2x lumber. Compared with the Makita XSH03Z it costs much less and comes in a complete kit. It lacks platform support, so batteries are proprietary.

Treat it as a light duty saw. Replace the stock blade with a better one for cleaner cuts. Because it is a kit, it works out of the box, but plan to replace the stock blade.
products.bestFor: Light projects where a complete kit matters more than platform.
pros: Two 4.0 Ah batteries in the kit

buyingCriteria.criterion: Blade size and depth of cut
buyingCriteria.explanation: A 7-1/4 inch blade cuts about 2-9/16 inches deep at 90 degrees, enough for a 4x4 in one pass, as on the DeWalt DCS590B. A 6-1/2 inch blade is lighter but cuts shallower, near 2-1/4 inches, as on the unbranded kit. Cutting depth drops at 45 degrees. Match the blade to the thickest wood you cut. A frequent mistake is to forget that the blade teeth stick out past the shoe, so a 2-9/16 inch rating assumes the shoe sits flat on the work. Set depth about 1/4 inch deeper than the board for the cleanest, safest cut.

Brushless motors run cooler and deliver more cuts per charge. The DeWalt DCS590B quotes up to 1,700 MWO and the Craftsman CMCS551B claims 75 percent more power than a brushed saw. Brushed saws are rare now. Brushless is the baseline. Judge power by the work, not the label: if the saw slows in wet 2x lumber or bogs in a bevel cut, it is under powered for that job. Brushless electronics also sense load and feed more current when the blade slows.

A battery saw is only as good as its pack, and a 2 Ah pack empties quickly in dense wood. A 5 Ah or FlexVolt pack gives much longer cuts. The DeWalt DCS578B uses FlexVolt batteries, while the others use 18V or 20V packs. Buy into a platform you will keep. A 5 Ah pack weighs about a pound more than a 2 Ah pack, and you feel it on a long overhead cut. Keep a second pack charging so you never run a cold or empty pack through dense wood.

A bevel capacity of 56 to 57 degrees allows steep angles, as on the Craftsman CMCS551B and DeWalt DCS578B. Positive stops at 22.5 and 45 degrees make setup quick. Cheaper saws have fewer stops. Check that the shoe locks firmly. Cutting a 45 degree bevel in 2x lumber needs about 1-1/2 inches at 90 degrees plus extra for the bevel, so check depth at your most used angle. Wide shoe plates also keep the saw stable.

An electric brake stops the blade within a second or two after you release the trigger, as on the Milwaukee and DeWalt FlexVolt saws. It reduces risk and saves time. Look for a blade guard that returns smoothly. Never wedge the guard open. Kickback happens when the blade pinches, so a saw with a good guard and brake helps. Always support the offcut and keep your hands clear of the blade path.

A 7-1/4 inch saw with a large battery weighs about 9 to 11 lb, and that matters in long cuts. The 6-1/2 inch Makita XSH03Z is lighter. For overhead or one handed work, favor a lighter saw. For ripping, weight helps stability. Hold the saw on a scrap board and feel the balance before buying. A saw that tips forward off the cut is tiring all day.

specDecoder.meaning: A DeWalt measure of the saw's mechanical output. The DCS590B quotes up to 1,700 MWO. It is a peak figure, not continuous.
specDecoder.watchFor: MWO is not comparable across brands.

specDecoder.meaning: Blade speed with no cutting, such as 5,500 on the DCS590B and 7,000 on the unbranded kit. It drops under load.
specDecoder.watchFor: High rpm with a weak motor stalls in wet lumber.

specDecoder.meaning: The maximum cut depth with the shoe flat, such as 2-9/16 inches on the 7-1/4 inch saws. It tells you if you can cut a 4x4.
A DeWalt battery that works at 20V and 60V. It adds power and runtime to compatible tools.
specDecoder.watchFor: FlexVolt packs are costly and heavy.

specDecoder.meaning: A circuit that stops the blade quickly after the trigger is released. It reduces coast time.
specDecoder.watchFor: Not all budget saws have one.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cutting capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared blade size and depth, from 2-9/16 inches on the 7-1/4 inch saws to 2-1/4 inches on the unbranded kit. Larger capacity ranked higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motor and power
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at brushless motors and rated power, with the DCS590B at 1,700 MWO and FlexVolt DCS578B at 47 percent more than its predecessor.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery and runtime
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered capacity and platform support. The unbranded kit includes two 4.0 Ah packs. Others are bare tools.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety and features
howWeEvaluated.description: We credited electric brakes, bevel stops and LED lights.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The DCS590B leads overall, the DCS578B for power and the Craftsman for value. Makita is the light pick.

cards.label: 7-1/4 inch
cards.text: Deeper cuts and more power, but heavier. The DeWalt DCS590B, DCS578B, Milwaukee M18 and Craftsman fit here.

cards.label: 6-1/2 inch
cards.text: Lighter and handier, with less depth. The Makita XSH03Z and the unbranded kit fit here.

howToChoose.note: Choose 7-1/4 inch for framing and 6-1/2 inch for trim and plywood.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A thin kerf blade, good bevel stops and a light saw. Decking is cut in short crosscuts, which suits battery saws. Plywood needs a fine tooth blade.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Makita XSH03Z and Craftsman CMCS551B suit decking. The DeWalt DCS590B handles heavier cuts.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You cut lumber daily or need FlexVolt power. The DeWalt DCS590B or DCS578B repays the cost.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You cut a few boards a year. The Craftsman CMCS551B or the unbranded kit is enough.

maintenance.why: A dull blade strains the motor and drains batteries. Replace it before it wears the motor.
Sawdust sticks the guard. A clean guard returns smoothly.
A slow brake means worn parts. Replace the tool if it fails.
A loose lock shifts the angle mid cut.

faq.q: Is a cordless circular saw as powerful as a corded one?
faq.a: Top brushless models come close. Corded saws still win for sustained rips.

faq.q: What blade size should I choose?
faq.a: A 7-1/4 inch blade suits framing, while 6-1/2 inch is lighter for trim and plywood.

faq.q: How long does the battery last?
faq.a: It depends on wood thickness and pack size. A 5 Ah pack may cut dozens of 2x4 crosscuts.

faq.q: Do I need a FlexVolt saw?
faq.a: Only for heavy use. The DCS590B handles most work.
It is a safety feature that saves time. Look for one if you cut often.

faq.q: Can I cut metal with it?
faq.a: Only with the right blade and a saw designed for it. Wood blades are unsafe on metal.
